title: ErrorCatalog
description: A data file of error codes (an `errors.json` beside a group's schemas): one entry per code, with its HTTP status, whether a retry can succeed, who can fix it and what the person who meets it can do next. The generator emits it as typed constants (`ERROR_CODES`) in every target, so no language hand-copies a code.

wirePrefix.description: Prepended to a code on the wire (the HTTP error body's `code`); readers strip it.

status.description: The HTTP status the code is answered with; null where it never travels as an HTTP answer (a tool result, an internal signal).

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed later without anyone changing anything.

group.description: Codes one handler treats alike (one error class, one refusal family).

aliases.description: Older wire names of the same cause, kept where they are already answered.

NextAction.description: What the person who meets the code can do next (UX-06), in plain language: no codes, ids or field names. `kind` lets a client offer the matching control; `text` is the English words for clients without their own (the web app words each kind in the reader's language).

NextActionKind.description: The kind of step a person can take. none: nothing, the system carries on or there is nothing left to do; retry: send it again now; wait_then_retry: wait, then try again; reload: reload to see the current state, then act on it; change_request: change what was asked or entered (another model, a smaller file, a fixed field); new_conversation: start a new chat or continue privately; reconnect: connect or add the account it needs; ask_owner: ask the conversation's, agent's or object's owner; ask_admin: ask an admin; internal: never shown to a person, a service-to-service answer whose text says what the system does.

codes.meaning: The object changed since it was read.

nextAction.text: Reload to see the latest version, then make your change again.

codes.meaning: An internal signal; never answered over HTTP.

nextAction.text: Nothing to do: the service reads the object again and retries.
